analysis.title: GS Basics - Risk Reduction. Week Ahead. Cloud Revenue Growth.
key_insights: Markets rebounded from a weak end to last week. KOSPI +2%, Tokyo Electron +5% after beating numbers and guiding to 87% operating profit growth. Oil fell 3% as diplomatic channels stay open. Kioxia fell another 15%, so the rebound is not indiscriminate.

The central debate is whether AI economics are deteriorating or crowded positions are being forcibly liquidated. Privorotsky leans toward de-risking of crowded positions, noting nothing in last week's hyperscaler results suggested spending intentions were weakening, if anything the opposite.

Hyperscaler cloud growth delivered: Azure +48%, AWS +39%, Google Cloud +103%. Negative FCF, equity capital raises and rising leverage requirements raise questions about returns on capital, and the return on the next trillion dollars of investment is less certain than demand.

Intel fell 29% on Friday. Privorotsky reads Intel's warning as being about consumer PCs, margins and manufacturing rather than AI demand. Amazon went from down 7% pre-market to close down 1.4% despite FCF concerns. AMD reports tomorrow and is seen as critical after Intel.

The AI debate is described as circular: one side says power and data center build-out cannot keep up with 2027 spending, so picks-and-shovels growth rolls over and multiples compress. The other side says compute will be overproduced, destroying rental economics and also lowering multiples.

Positioning has been reset. The GS Equity Systematic L/S Performance Estimate fell 2.17% on the week, the worst weekly drawdown since Dec 2023. Fundamental L/S net exposure recovered to only the seventh percentile, largely through index short covering. AAII Bull-Bear is negative again and CNN fear/greed is in the 20s.

Prime book flows: single stocks were net sold for a 7th straight week, driven by long sales. Macro products were net bought for a 2nd straight week, driven by long buys and to a lesser extent short covers.

US midterms are tomorrow. Historically the period after midterms has been positive for equities, with removal of uncertainty often mattering more than the outcome. Much of the worry is already in positioning.

Iran: diplomacy through Qatar continued over the weekend and negotiations remain alive, but there is no agreement and the range of outcomes is wide. It is unclear whether the diplomatic window survives the elections. Privorotsky has little conviction.

Treasury QRA on Wednesday may be underappreciated. The question is whether Treasury offers duration relief through smaller long-end auctions, more buybacks or a shift toward bills. Long-end cuts were not explicitly raised in the dealer questionnaire, so an immediate reduction is less certain. A constructive surprise could help duration and growth equities, while unchanged issuance might disappoint at the margin.

BoE: Thursday's 25bp hike to 4% is almost fully priced. The question is whether Bailey validates the three to four more hikes priced over the next year. Privorotsky leans toward the market overpricing the full tightening cycle given weakening growth, with energy inflation the main risk.

Last week looked like wholesale de-grossing: momentum unwinding, most-shorted names squeezing, leverage leaving the system, with defensives and quality strong while AI multiples compressed. The market is pricing an abrupt growth slowdown, stalled AI capex, lower nominal growth and rates, and a premium for quality balance sheets.

Privorotsky's gut view is a year-end rally that is under-owned, poorly participated in and hard to chase. Friday felt like capitulation, but risk will be added only after the coming events are cleared.

Busy week: ISM manufacturing and Apple tonight (iPhone demand, early Duo orders), AMD tomorrow, Arista as a read on AI networking, and Friday NFP with consensus around +65k, unemployment 4.2% and wages +0.3%.

sector_views.rationale: Demand is strong, but returns on the next trillion dollars of investment are uncertain and crowded positioning turns each concern into a reason to de-risk.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscaler cloud growth delivered (Azure +48%, AWS +39%, Google Cloud +103%) and nothing in last week's results suggested spending intentions were weakening. AI monetization continues to improve, and positioning is now cleaner.
tension_points.bear_case: Negative FCF, equity capital raises and growing leverage requirements raise questions about returns on capital, and the return on the next trillion dollars of investment is much less certain.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A weak AMD print tomorrow after Intel's warning, or signs of hyperscalers cutting spending intentions.

tension_points.what_invalidates: Disappointing event outcomes this week (midterms, Treasury QRA, BoE, NFP) that keep investors from adding risk.
